card.one_liner: Save offers without over-promising, early termination fees that are actually waivable, and when to stop the script.

rules.text: Retention offers above 40% off require supervisor sign-off.
An early termination fee is prorated by remaining months of the contract.
One late fee waiver per 12 months on an account in good standing.
Confirm whether the customer has already activated with another carrier before any save offer.

exceptions.text: The early termination fee is waived when the customer moves to an address with no coverage; a utility bill at the new address is enough proof.
A customer within 30 days of contract end pays no termination fee even though the system still quotes one; override and note it.
An autopay failure caused by a card reissue, with the bank letter, resets the late-fee counter for that cycle.
If the customer already ported out, skip the save script and quote only the final prorated bill; the script costs 3 minutes and produces a complaint.

judgment_calls.text: Offer the 40% retention tier only when the customer names a competitor's price; otherwise start at 15% and hold.
A customer calling for the third time in 30 days about the same fee gets the waiver on the spot; the call cost exceeds the fee.
A fee dispute over 100 dollars with any prior credit on the account goes to the billing desk, not retention.

common_mistakes.text: Reading the full save script to a customer who has already switched, generating an escalation.
Quoting the system's termination fee at day 25 of a 30-day end-of-contract window.
Promising a 40% offer before supervisor sign-off; audit reverses it and the customer calls back.

never_do.text: Never waive a second late fee in 12 months without a documented bank failure; refuse and offer autopay setup instead.
Never run the save script on a customer who has confirmed a port-out.
Never quote an early termination fee without checking the contract end date first.
